top_choice_rationale: P001 credits the invention (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice) and its decisive realization at about 1e-18 (Ye), a two-name allocation that fits the real division of labour. The performance is reproduced independently at RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and NPL and checked against an external standard, so the result is mature and not interpretive. The citation can be kept distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes by naming the neutral-atom lattice. The remaining reservations (Paris, PTB, NIST and single-ion contributions, the pending SI second) are framing and boundary questions, not defects in the science. P002 is a genuine and mature achievement but its credit gap (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu) is unresolved, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. My PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur work is astroparticle physics and not in this slate.
